english: O great, bright Father Dyeus, listen! You who split the vault of heaven, we praise you. You who set the stars, we sing to you. You who freed the waters, we pray to you. Your great fame has reached the gods. We trust in you and do not fear death (sleep). Watch over our works from above. May our bulls and sheep grow strong. May our warriors be swift. May the wolf not come to our fences. O Bhagos (dispenser), we give you this song. Hear it and accept it.
uncertain: h₂éḱmonm̥: 'stone' / 'heavenly vault'; chose the vault of heaven
supnṓd: ABL of supnos 'sleep; death', i.e. 'not afraid of sleep/death'
bʰáge: VOC 'allotter, god': an epithet of Dyeus or a separate god Bhagos
gʷéHyomes: lexicon gloss empty; root geH- 'sing, cry'

english: Dawn, bright daughter of Dyeus, shine forth! You who drove the darkness away, we sing to you. Night, your sister, has gone away with the stars. You have come to us on a swift chariot. You wear light and splendor. You stride through the middle of the sky. You clothe the branches with brightness. The east and the sea are red. The bulls have woken and look at you. Dawn, bring us livestock. Do not hide your brightness from us. May you shine for us and our brothers. Dawn, we sing to you in our hearts.
uncertain: n̥sméy nos: 1PL dative written twice ('for us ... for us')

english: Seven sisters, waters, listen to us! You go along seven paths to the sea. The salty sea receives you. Cattle and dogs drink you. Fire (Agni) was born of you; Fire dwells in your waters. You are the mothers of famous Agni. The serpent swallowed you, and the earth dried up. The slayer split the serpent, and you came out into the light again. Sisters, go to our fields! Nourish seed and roots. May this year's grain grow full.
uncertain: h₁áyto: MID AOR of h₁ay- 'take, receive'
bʰéh₂os h₂ew h₁n̥dʰté: 'came forth again (into) the light'; bʰéh₂os has no case marking (NOM/ACC)

english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep! We see this, and it pains our heart: man, the master, weaves the sheep's wool into a warm garment for himself, and the sheep have no wool."
uncertain: different orthography (Schleicher-fable style): tu 'and/then', h₂owey VOC 'sheep', agʰnutór 'is pained', dʰǵʰémō 'man', sē 'for himself', gʷʰérmom 'warm', wept 'wove/makes' (webʰ- 'weave'); several forms not analyzed

english: Earth, mother of the gods, we praise you. Dyeus is above, and you are below. He gives light; you give seed. Our fathers died, and you received them. Now they lie within, asleep. You shelter them from sun and wind. You guard their long sleep. Earth, remember them, and remember us! Give us offspring and wool. May our livestock and offspring increase. May our name be famous among warriors. Broad one, we offer you portions.
uncertain: h₂óytons: 'portions, what is given' (marked uncertain in the lexicon)

english: The sheep and the horses.
uncertain: laryngeal-less orthography, not analyzed: owis 'sheep', eḱwōs 'horses', kʷe 'and'; a title

english: Dawn, daughter of Dyeus, we sing to you. Night is your sister; she clothes the earth. When you come with light, she departs. You light her up with splendor. She follows you, and you follow her. You found the cattle hidden in darkness. You drove them out and led them to the fields. Then the gods were astonished and rejoiced. Now, Dawn, we pray to you. Lead us and our brothers to the light. Guard our fences from the wolf. May your brightness not leave us.
uncertain: dukdʰí nos n̥smé: 1PL object written twice (enclitic nos and tonic n̥smé)
h₁régʷesi: LOC 'in darkness' (also read as SBJV of h₁regʷ-)

english: Dyeus, father of the gods, we praise you. We call on your famous name. You set seven stars in the sky. You set the sun on its course. You gave light to the sun. Now night is gone; Dawn, your daughter, has come. She brings us bright light. The stars have vanished, and the warriors have woken. Protect our horses and sheep. May the wolf not seize them from the fields. Give us good fame. May we see the sun; may our offspring live.
uncertain: dʰéh₁s: AOR.2SG 'you placed' (could also be NOM 'god'); verb fits
h₂ḱméni: LOC 'in the (stone) vault of heaven'

english: Swift waters, I have come to you. There is a stain in my heart. I broke an oath; the two gods saw it. Now I fear them. Waters, carry the stain away from me. Clothe me with your water. I stand bare in your waters. I give you butter and wine. Daughters of Dyeus, accept these things. May the gods not see my stain. May my mind be free of the stain. I praise you and invoke your works.
uncertain: tóybʰos: plural 'them' for the two gods
misfit: kʷḱént: AOR.3PL with dual subject deywóh₁ (3DU expected)

english: Dawn, daughter of Dyeus, where are you? The night is long and heavy for us. Widows are afraid; dogs are afraid. We long to see your light and brightness. Darkness was swallowing the sun and the stars. You split it with your splendor and light. Then the sun came out of it. Dawn, you came forth in the east. You spread your light over the fields. Dawn, come back to us; do not go away from us. We, your praisers, sing you a song. Dawn, your fame is imperishable.
uncertain: bʰéyds toy tód: toy read as 'your' (splendor) or ethic dative; tód = the darkness (neuter)

english: Father Dyeus, you thunder above. Your thunder is great and heavy. The earth trembles and the sea trembles. The cattle in the fields are afraid. Your wind stirs the sea. The crawling serpent was hiding the waters. You struck the serpent with thunder and freed the waters for us. Now the waters run down onto the earth. Slayer, we sing to you and praise you. Do not slay our warriors in battle. Guard our fields and fences. May your fame be imperishable.
uncertain: sérpontih₂: fem participle; agrees with h₁ógʷʰis, which the lexicon lists as feminine
dʰéǵʰōm ní yéh₂ti: 'go down to the earth'

english: Mother Earth, you stand beneath the sky. You do not tremble at heavy thunder. Your beavers live in the waters. Your grain nourishes us. We stand at your navel. We light a fire there. We speak good words there. The waters clothed you; the gods lifted you up. They gave you a famous name, and you rejoiced. You became broad and great. May you stand firm for us and for our offspring. Give us livestock and imperishable fame.

Sun, you go beneath the earth to the dead. The dead lie there in sleep. You alone among the gods have seen them. You light up their long sleep. Then you come out of the waters toward the east. You follow Dawn on her course. Your light has reached the fields. Beavers swim in the waters. Your wheel turns and does not break. Sun, do not burn our seed. May our ears of grain be heavy and good. Give light to the dead.
uncertain: h₂éwsterōy: DAT 'toward the east' (elsewhere LOC h₂éwsteroy)

english: Dawn, I woke in the darkness. I lit the fire for the gods. I prepared butter and wine. Now I sing to you and pray to you. Come forth, bright daughter of Dyeus! Light up my paths and fences. Put brightness into my heart. Drive the wolf away from my sheep. Give me livestock and strength. I offer you this song. May I and my brother see you. Dawn, do not leave me; come again.
misfit: kʷḱyéh₁m̥: OPT.1SG with a coordinated subject 'I and my brother' (h₁eǵ ... bʰréh₂tēr-kʷe); 1DU expected

english: Dyeus, our father, hear our words. Giver of good things, we sing to you. You hold up the broad sky. You are great among the gods. You split the vault of heaven with heavy thunder, and the waters came out of it. The broad earth drank the water. You watch over us from above. You know the long paths of the stars. Our hearts and minds are turned to you. Dogs fear your thunder. Give us swift horses. Guard our sheep from the wolf. May our fame be imperishable. Bright one, listen to our song.
uncertain: ḱwónes toy gʰrómōd: toy read as 'your (thunder)'
nos (with wékʷōs): 'our words'; with no pronoun on wékʷōs in the first clause, nos may go with ph₂tér

english: Then the sheep said to the horses: "My heart is pained, seeing a man driving horses."
uncertain: Schleicher-style orthography, mostly not analyzed: eḱwobʰ(y)os / eḱwomos (variant DAT.PL 'to the horses'), ewewkʷet 'said', agʰnutoi 'is pained', aǵontm̥ 'driving', nerm̥ 'man', widn̥tei 'seeing/to (me) seeing'

english: Agni, carrier of our songs, listen! Praisers call on you. Agni, you know the long ways. Carry our song to Dyeus and to Bhagos. Carry butter to Dawn. Carry grain to the Sun. May the gods be satisfied with our offerings. You went to the gods and brought their word to us. Your fire glows for the gods. Give us imperishable fame. May we live in your light. Agni, we sing your famous name.
uncertain: diwéy bʰágōy: two datives 'to Dyeus, (to) Bhagos', or 'to Dyeus the allotter'

english: Agni, I bring you butter. I prepared it for you with my own hands. I give you grain; I sing you a song. Agni, accept these things and carry them to the gods. You are the carrier of our offerings. I ask you for cattle and livestock. I ask for offspring and fame. Agni, give them to me in return. Guard me from the wolf and from the terrible one. Agni, do not burn me or my brother. I am your praiser, and you are my god. May I see the dawn and the sun again.
uncertain: h₂m̥bʰí: 'around / in exchange for'; chose 'in return'
mē h₁éwses: prohibitive with PST 2SG 'do not burn'

english: Broad one, Mother Earth, we sing to you. You bear cattle and horses. You bear the waters and the sea. You bear roots and seeds. Your navel lies in the middle. The dead lie there beside you. Who created you, broad one, and your fields? The gods made you with their hands. Earth, you are fruitful and you nourish us. Dyeus gave you seed; grain grew from you. Nourish our bulls; may our ears of grain grow. When our breath departs, receive us.

Sun, you know the ways; you do not go astray. I am going to my brother on a long road. Snakes and thorns are on it. Go before me and light it up for me. Protect my steps with your brightness. May I not slip from it. May wolves and dogs not see me. May I get there, and may he see me. My mother prays to you. My sister sits by the fire. May I come back to them with wealth. Sun, I will give you wine.
uncertain: tā́s: fem ACC.PL 'them', presumably mother and sister (a pair, written as plural)

english: Gods, givers of good things, come to us! Sit in the middle and drink wine. Gods, rejoice in your hearts. Father Dyeus, come with Dawn, your daughter. Agni, bring the sun and the waters. Earth, our mother, listen. You gods slew the serpent with thunder. You freed the waters and the cattle from the rock. You set the sun and the stars above. Now we sing your great fame. Give us might and strength. Protect us from the wolf and from sores. Your strength is imperishable.
uncertain: gʷʰn̥té: PRS/PST 2PL 'you slay/were slaying' (not an aorist), in a row of aorists

english: Dawn, you have come; the darkness is gone. Dawn, you are our light. You shine on the sea and in the waters. You shine on the roots and the branches. You shine on the gods and on the dead. Shine for us, Dawn, shine for us and our brothers. When you flashed up, the gods rejoiced; they sang you a song. Now we sing this song to you again. Daughter of Dyeus, accept our words. Give us might and fame. May we be free from fear. Bright one, we praise you in our hearts.
uncertain: tórgʷōd h₁léwdʰerōs: 'free from the terrible one / from terror'

english: Mother Earth, your fields are broad. Your sheep give wool. Your bulls are swift and heavy. We milk your cows; we eat your grain. We drink your water, and it gladdens our hearts. What do we offer you in return? We offer you songs and butter in return. Dyeus saw you and came to love you. The gods were born of you and Dyeus. The gods stand at your navel. Protect our offspring and sheep. Earth, hear our words.
uncertain: ḱérdh₂-kʷe nos méwdt: AOR.3SG 'our hearts rejoiced' (neuter plural subject with singular verb)
te ... twé: 2SG object written twice (one for each verb)
misfit: deywṓm: GEN.PL 'of the gods' standing as subject of ǵeǵn̥h₁ḗr (PRF.3PL 'were born'); NOM.PL deywṓs expected

english: Dawn, come to us with light. You light up the long paths. You light up the broad earth. You light up the sea. Night yields the sky to you. Dyeus gave you a famous name. Dawn, he set you on your course. You come again, and the dogs have woken. Warriors yoke the chariots. Dawn, give us livestock and wool. May we see your light and splendor again. Dawn, do not leave us in darkness.
uncertain: h₂éwsos toy twé h₁iméni dʰéh₁t: subject = Dyeus (from the sentence before); h₂éwsos is VOC
misfit: lowkéyonti: PRS.3PL with subject túH 'you (sg.)'; 2SG lowkéyesi expected (as in the next two sentences)

english: Gods of heaven, we praise you. Dyeus, your father, is great. Earth is your mother. Dawn is your sister. Agni carries our offerings to you. The Sun has seen our works. Darkness lay in the waters. You split it with light and radiance. Dawn came forth and the sun shone. Now the cattle live, and the waters live. Gods, do not abandon us. Give us splendor and livestock.
uncertain: diwés deywṓs: 'gods of the sky' (GEN diwés + VOC.PL)
méǵh₂s wos dyḗws ph₂tḗr h₁ésti: 'your father Dyeus is great' or 'great Dyeus is your father'

english: "Who are you, bright and swift ones?" "We are the waters, daughters of Dyeus." "Where do you go on your courses?" "We go down to the salty sea." "What do you carry in your waters?" "We carry stains away." "What do you give to the roots, sisters?" "We give water to the roots." Daughters of Dyeus, we pray to you. Carry our stains away. Nourish our offspring and swift horses. Sisters, may you not dry up for us.
uncertain: mē tr̥sih₁té: OPT.2PL with mē, 'may you not dry up'

english: Agni, giver of good things, we sing to you. You were born of the waters. You carry our offerings to the gods. Agni, you speak to the gods for us. You lick the butter, and your fire burns. You were hiding in the branches. The gods searched for you and found you. They brought you out and set you in the middle. Agni, bring them to us. May they sit down and drink wine. Agni, guard our sleep and our fences. Swift Agni, do not burn us.
uncertain: kʷḱént: 'saw, caught sight of', i.e. found

english: Gods, I am your warrior. I go to war with my brothers. My two horses draw the chariot. My heart and mind do not tremble. Gods, protect me in war. May I not die there; may I not fall there. May I overcome the warriors with my strength. May wolves and dogs eat the dead. You overcame the serpent; Father Dyeus struck it with thunder. Give me victory in war. If I come back, I will give you seven cows. May my fame be imperishable.
uncertain: tā́m: fem ACC 'it' = the serpent (h₁ógʷʰis is feminine in the lexicon)
